sources.citation: WALS Online, language Mbara (wals_code mbr), values coded from Tourneux et al. 1986.
sources.note: Only morphology/word-order features (citing pp. 148-194); no values for 13A tone or 14A-17A stress features.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. Utrecht: LOT (375).
sources.note: Sec. 5.3.3 Musgum group uses Mbara data (771-entry word list from Tourneux et al. 1986; vowel harmony prosodies, two underlying vowels); author states his reconstructions/sketches do 'not includ[e] tone or stress'; nothing on Mbara stress.

sources.citation: Lanne, Bernard. 1990. Review of Tourneux, Seignobos & Lafarge, Les Mbara et leur langue. Revue française d'histoire d'outre-mer 77(286): 138-139.
sources.note: Says Tourneux's linguistic part contains demographic notes, four tales and two lexicons; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Boulègue, Jean. 1988. Review of Tourneux, Seignobos & Lafarge, Les Mbara et leur langue (Tchad). Journal des Africanistes 58(1): 153-154.
sources.note: Review (p.153 text read) discusses only Seignobos's historical part; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 1978. Le mulwi de Mogroum (Tchad): phonologie, éléments de grammaire. Thèse de 3e cycle, Paris 3 (HAL tel-02372418).
sources.note: Describes Mulwi (Musgu), not Mbara; Mbara mentioned only as neighbours and as the informant's mother tongue ('mbéré'); no Mbara phonology.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 1978. Première note sur le mbara. Africana Marburgensia XI(2): 27-32.
